title: Shadwell and Talbott — family promises and requested conduct
shortTitle: Shadwell and Talbott — family promises and requested c…
summary: The notes use family arrangements to test whether an act is the agreed price of a promise.
notes: The distinction is between actual reciprocal inducement and conduct the promisor merely welcomes or predicts. The presence of a family relationship does not answer whether a bargain exists.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 59–60. Open assigned page 59.
